methods.name: MintUserToken
methods.description:
Mint a user token for a person signed in to an organization's own product.

 The product's backend calls it with a service account's API key and the
 person's identity, as it would call any server API with its key. Stigmer
 resolves the person's identity account in the organization the token is
 for, creates it on first sign-in when the organization's embedding
 settings allow (granting their sign_in_role), and returns a token bound
 to that organization. A token for a child organization works in that
 child only; one for the service account's own organization also reaches
 its child organizations, only as far as the person's role there allows.

 Only a service account's key may mint, and only one whose account is an
 administrator of the organization the token is for, or of its parent
 organization: minting can create accounts and grant a role. A person's
 key or token is refused PERMISSION_DENIED.

 The token lives until it expires or until the service account that
 minted it is deleted, whichever comes first. Rotating the account's key
 leaves minted tokens working.

 Error scenarios:
 - PERMISSION_DENIED: the caller is not a service account, or its account
   may not mint for the organization.
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the person has no account and the organization's
   embedding settings do not create one, or the server does not
   authenticate its callers.
 - INTERNAL: account provisioning could not be completed. No partial
   account is left behind, so the request is safe to retry: a retry
   completes the provisioning.

 Origin enforcement (OrganizationEmbedding.allowed_origins) does not apply
 to this call: minting is server-to-server, so there is no browser Origin
 to check. It applies to the browser requests that bear the minted token.

methods.name: MintGuestToken
methods.description:
Mint a guest token for an anonymous visitor of an agent's chat link.

 Resolves the channel id from the hosted chat link to a web channel and
 returns a short-lived token scoped to that channel's organization.
 Editions that do not host chat-link pages answer it UNIMPLEMENTED.

methodTypes.name: MintUserTokenRequest
methodTypes.description:
MintUserTokenRequest names the organization and the person a user token
 is for.

 Sent from the product's backend, never from a browser: it carries the
 service account's API key.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
The organization the token is for, by id or slug: the minting service
 account's organization, or one of its child organizations. The person's
 account, their first sign-in and the token are all in this organization.

fields.name: UserId
fields.description:
The product's stable identifier for the person. With org it names one
 identity account (keyed "stgm_pc|{org}|{user_id}"), so the same user_id
 in two organizations is two accounts.

 Must be stable for the person: changing it creates a new identity
 account. It must not contain the separator character '|'.

fields.name: UserEmail
fields.description:
The person's email address, as the product knows it. Used when the
 account is created; later mints do not change the stored profile.

fields.name: UserName
fields.description:
The person's display name, as the product knows it. Used when the
 account is created; later mints do not change the stored profile.

methodTypes.name: MintUserTokenResponse
methodTypes.description: MintUserTokenResponse holds the minted token and its lifetime.

fields.name: AccessToken
fields.description:
The token the browser sends as its Bearer credential. Pass it to the
 React SDK's StigmerProvider through getAccessToken.

fields.name: ExpiresIn
fields.description: Token lifetime in seconds from the time of issuance.

methodTypes.name: MintGuestTokenRequest
methodTypes.description: MintGuestTokenRequest identifies a chat link and optional visitor cookie id.

fields.name: ChannelId
fields.description: Id of the web channel, from the hosted chat link (required).

fields.name: GuestCookieId
fields.description:
Per-browser visitor cookie id from a prior mint (optional).

 When empty, the server generates a high-entropy id and returns it so the
 hosted page can persist it in an httpOnly cookie. When supplied, it must
 be the value previously returned by this RPC for the same visitor.

fields.name: EmbedOrigin
fields.description:
Web origin of the page embedding the chat (optional).

 Set by the hosted chat page when it runs inside an iframe (the embedding
 page's origin, e.g. "https://docs.example.com") and by direct SDK embeds
 (their own page origin). Leave empty on the unframed hosted page. The
 literal value "null" reports a framed page whose parent origin could not
 be determined (opaque origin).

fields.name: LinkToken
fields.description:
Link token from the chat link's `?k=` parameter (optional).

 Required when the chat link has been locked with rotateLink; ignored
 for plain chat links.

methodTypes.name: MintGuestTokenResponse
methodTypes.description: MintGuestTokenResponse contains the guest JWT and the visitor cookie id.

fields.name: AccessToken
fields.description: Stigmer-signed JWT for authenticating a chat link visitor's API calls.

fields.name: ExpiresIn
fields.description: Token lifetime in seconds from the time of issuance.

fields.name: GuestCookieId
fields.description:
Visitor cookie id to persist client-side, as an httpOnly cookie.

 Echoes guest_cookie_id from the request when provided; otherwise a newly
 generated high-entropy value.
